answer: Calibrate the penalty, not just the gate. Size the slashable bond per identity so detection probability times the forfeited deposit exceeds the most a fake could earn before being caught. The inlet to minting costs an opal-hard deposit, burned in full on any audit failure. Each added name then carries negative expected value, a yarrow of losing bets; an honest agent never fails audit and never pays. Breadth stops paying because every extra identity raises expected loss faster than expected gain.
